Where value is actually created

Most of the value on a development scheme is created between acquisition and planning consent, not during construction. Sites bought right, with a planning strategy that lands within the borough's Local Plan, refinance or sell at the assumed GDV. Sites bought against a wishlist planning position leak value at every stage: extended determination, reduced consented density, s.106 obligations that were not modelled, and delivery to a spec that the exit case cannot support.

The design-and-delivery half then has to hold the assumed programme and cost. That requires one team accountable across pre-construction and construction; a fully coordinated design at tender, not at contract; and a QS discipline that reports to the funder on the same schedule the funder needs to release drawdowns. When those two halves connect, the scheme lands close to plan.

How we deliver, in order

  1. Site sourcingIntroducer network, off-market and on-market opportunities screened against the client's target return, hold period and postcode.
  2. UnderwritingIRR, MOIC, refi and exit sensitivity, funding cost and drawdown schedule modelled against realistic contingency.
  3. Planning & concept designPre-application, concept massing, unit mix and initial cost plan tested with the borough before a formal submission.
  4. Planning submissionFull planning application with the required documents (design and access, heritage where applicable, transport, ecology, drainage, energy).
  5. Funding / JV agreementDebt coordinated with the senior lender's monitoring surveyor; JV or equity documents finalised where applicable.
  6. Tender or negotiationTwo-stage tender or negotiated route, priced against the coordinated design not a Stage 2 sketch.
  7. ConstructionEnabling works through superstructure to fit-out, on one programme owned by one team.
  8. PC, letting, refi or exitHandover, warranty pack, marketing pack for the letting agent, and refinance drawdown or sale.

Frequently asked questions

Do you take equity?

On selected schemes, yes. We co-invest as an equity partner in a special-purpose vehicle where the numbers, the sponsor and the exit align. The delivery contract (JCT or bespoke) is a separate agreement from the equity holding so the two risks are not commingled and any conflict is transparent to any other equity partner or lender.

What JV structures do you work with?

Standard SPV structures (Ltd, LLP, occasionally offshore where the sponsor's tax position requires) with an equity waterfall (pref return, catch-up, promote) agreed at the shareholders' agreement stage. We do not pool retail investor money, and every JV is between sophisticated or professional counterparties acting on their own advice.

What is planning-risk shopping?

Screening a longlist of sites against the applicable Local Plan and any recent appeal decisions, to score each site's planning risk before an offer is made. This distinguishes sites where a workable planning position is a routine pre-application away from sites that need a public inquiry or Secretary of State call-in to deliver.

How do you separate GDV modelling from cost planning?

GDV is set from comparable evidence (recent sales and rents at that postcode for the target unit type) at Stage 1. The cost plan is set from the coordinated design. Where the two diverge, the design or spec is adjusted at Stage 2 or 3, not at tender. A scheme that only balances GDV and cost at tender has already lost the optimisation window.

Which procurement route do you recommend?

Depends on the scheme: two-stage tender with named subcontractors for cost certainty on a coordinated design; JCT Design & Build with novation for cost certainty and single-point risk on a mid-sized residential scheme; negotiated contract for repeat-client work with a settled supply chain. Traditional JCT Standard Building Contract with quantities remains right where the design is genuinely bespoke and the architect stays engaged through construction.

What warranties do lenders and buyers expect?

For residential sale: NHBC, LABC, BuildZone, ICW or CRL structural warranty; collateral warranties from the design team and key subcontractors to the funder and to any incoming purchaser; manufacturer warranties on the envelope and roof; and an EPC and gas safety certificate on completion.
